notes: Main disagreements: (1) modality on the committee charge items (A informs, B should), resolved as informs because the page reports what the committee was charged to do and does not instruct a reader; (2) actor and modality on the committee's recognition sentences, resolved by whom the sentence addresses (all) and whether it recommends (considering the normative questions is should); (3) policy_type on four units: the CTL statistic about student AI use (P55 vs UNCOVERED, resolved UNCOVERED because it is prevalence, not effects on learning), 'Respond appropriately if questions arise' (UNCOVERED vs P123, resolved P123 with the fit note), the committee's 'living framework' (P54 vs P56, resolved P54), and two SSOE violation items (P36 vs P22 for AI help in evaluations, resolved P22; P36 vs P04 for AI aid 'expressly prohibited by the instructor', resolved P04); (4) document stance on two of three documents: committee page (A delegates, B permit, resolved delegates because the page states a charge and no rule) and SSOE integrity policy (A delegates, B restrict, resolved delegates because only evaluations are barred by default and other AI aid is a violation only where the instructor prohibits it); (5) splitting and anchors: coder A merged the CTL 'Streamline your workload' tile into one unit while B split it into four (teaching, collaboration, productivity, research), B's units kept with imperative sentences recoded as should and anchored on the whole sentence; (6) B-only units: 7 CTL tile blurbs and 2 committee charge items were real and kept; 13 SSOE units on general hearing procedure, sanctions, board and appeal contain nothing on AI use and were dropped; A-only units: 2 committee passages (Points to Consider description, Mapping Project), both real and kept. Unit stance on SSOE disclosure item recoded require (A and B both restrict).
